about: Virginia city and county rules on camping or sleeping in public, one row per locality FIPS, each with a source. Checked 2026-10-24 by news and council-record search, not by reading every local code. A locality that is not listed was not checked; 'checked_none_found' means a search found no ordinance, which is NOT the same as 'allowed' (trespass, park-hours and loitering rules still apply). Statewide: HB1394 (2026), which would have barred localities from penalizing sleeping or resting in public, was continued to 2027 by a House subcommittee in February 2026, so local bans stand.

statuses.ban_citywide: Camping or sleeping on public property is a crime across the locality. Scored 0.
statuses.ban_partial: Banned in part of the locality (for example downtown sidewalks or public rights-of-way). Scored 35.
statuses.proposed_not_adopted: A ban was proposed and not adopted. Not scored: other rules can still be used to move people.
statuses.checked_none_found: Searched; no camping or sleeping ordinance found. Not scored.

state_note.text: Virginia has no statewide camping ban, and a 2026 bill to stop local bans (HB1394) was continued to 2027.
state_note.source_title: WHRO, 'Virginia House committee kills bill to decriminalize homelessness', 2026-02-08

51650.summary: No sleeping, camping or storing belongings on public property, including parks, beaches, schools and sidewalks. Police warn first and offer help; a summons comes only if the person refuses to leave.
51650.penalty: Class 2 misdemeanor: up to 6 months in jail and a $1,000 fine
51650.source_title: WHRO, 'Hampton bans camping and sleeping on public property', 2026-04-09; WAVY, 2026-04-10

51520.summary: Camping on city-owned streets, sidewalks, alleys and other public rights-of-way is banned (Ordinance 22-9).
51520.source_title: WSET, 'Bristol, Virginia City Council passes public camping ban', 2022-08-09

51770.summary: Camping on downtown sidewalks is banned; in effect since 2022.
51770.source_title: WSLS, 'Virginia bill could overturn Roanoke's homeless camping ban', 2026-02-04

51540.summary: A ban on sleeping, camping and storing belongings in public areas (Class 4 misdemeanor) was proposed by the police chief and tabled indefinitely by City Council in September 2025.
51540.source_title: Charlottesville Tomorrow, 'Charlottesville City Council tables proposed ordinance that would ban camping on city property', 2025-09

51121.summary: A news search on 2026-10-24 found no camping or sleeping ordinance for Montgomery County, Blacksburg or Christiansburg. Town and county codes were not read line by line.
